title: Jigsaw Puzzle Game in Flutter
description: A beautiful, interactive Jigsaw Puzzle game in Flutter featuring custom difficulty levels, dynamic image fetching via Pexels API, and an immersive glassmorphism UI.
overview: Jigsaw Puzzle Pro is a polished, mobile-first Flutter application built with a focus on immersive aesthetics and replayability. The app leverages the GetX ecosystem for smooth state management and integrates the Pexels API so users can generate puzzles from thousands of stunning online landscapes, alongside an integrated coin and daily reward system.
features: Dynamic image fetching using the Pexels API
Custom puzzles using local device gallery photos
Virtual coin system with daily login rewards
Relaxing background music and interactive sound effects
Immersive glassmorphism UI with smooth animations
challenges: Implementing dynamic grid slicing for various image aspect ratios and difficulties
Managing complex application state and routing smoothly using GetX
Securing and structuring API calls to Pexels without exposing environment variables
Optimizing the performance of glassmorphism UI layers alongside puzzle drag-and-drop mechanics
learnings: GetX significantly reduces boilerplate for state management, dependency injection, and routing
Using third-party APIs like Pexels creates endless, highly engaging dynamic content for casual games
Integrating subtle audio feedback and micro-animations massively improves the overall game feel

title: MotionComfort
description: An Android application designed to reduce motion sickness by displaying synchronized visual cues based on real-time device motion. Built with Jetpack Compose, custom overlay rendering, and sensor-driven interactions.
overview: MotionComfort is a sensor-based Android application that helps reduce motion sickness while using a smartphone in moving vehicles. The app uses accelerometer data to generate motion-synchronized visual cues such as floating particles and horizon lines, reducing the sensory conflict between visual perception and vestibular feedback.
features: Real-time motion synchronization using device sensors
challenges: Implementing Android overlay permissions across modern Android versions
Handling foreground service restrictions introduced in Android 14+
Creating smooth sensor-driven animations without affecting performance
Balancing visual cue responsiveness and user comfort
Managing touch-through overlays while rendering on top of other apps
learnings: Working with Android SensorManager and accelerometer data
Building foreground services with modern Android requirements
Designing reactive UIs using Jetpack Compose and StateFlow
Handling runtime permissions and system-level Android APIs
